question.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $G?$

I. $(H∨G)∧G$

II. $H∧(H∨G)$

III. $(G∨H)∨G$
question.worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
G∧(G∨H)≡G.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is logically equivalent to $G.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(H∨G)∧G & ≡G∧(H∨G) \\  & ≡G∧(G∨H) \\  & ≡G.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is *not* logically equivalent to $G.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}H∧(H∨G) & ≡H≢G.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is *not* logically equivalent to $G.$ This statement cannot be simplified using the absorption laws.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
